sections.text:
Isaac, peace be upon him, is the second son of Abraham Al-Khalil, peace be upon him, and his birth was a great divine miracle that astonished minds.

Abraham's wife, Mrs. Sarah, had reached a very old age and had become a childless old woman, and Abraham had also grown old and old.

At that time, angels (in the form of human guests) came to visit Abraham on their way to destroy Lot's people.

Abraham, the great and generous, welcomed them and offered them a roasted calf to eat, but they did not extend their hands to the food, and they became afraid.

They reassured him and told him that they were the angels of God, and gave him good news of the birth of a knowledgeable boy who would be one of the prophets, namely Isaac.

Lady Sarah heard this good news, and she frowned with great astonishment and said: “Woe to me, I will give birth when I am old, and this is my husband who is old. This is a strange thing.”

The angels responded to her, reminding her of God’s absolute power: “Do you marvel at God’s command? May God’s mercy and blessings be upon you, O People of the House.”

Isaac, peace be upon him, was born and was the apple of his eyes when they were old, and he was raised in the house of prophecy, monotheism, and generosity.

From his father Abraham, Isaac inherited forbearance, piety, and pure worship of God Almighty.

God chose him to be a prophet and messenger to the people of the Levant and Palestine, to complete his father’s path in spreading monotheism and fighting polytheism.

Isaac married and God blessed him with twins, one of whom was the Prophet Jacob, peace be upon him, who was nicknamed “Israel.”

Hence, Isaac, peace be upon him, became the father of all the prophets of the Children of Israel who came after him, such as Joseph, Moses, David, Solomon, and Jesus, peace be upon them all.

Therefore, Isaac is known as the trunk of the tree of the prophets on the part of the Children of Israel, just as his brother Ishmael was the trunk of the Arab branch and the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

Isaac was a good man, very devout, just in his rule among people, upholding God’s law and spreading goodness on earth.

God praised him in the Holy Qur’an along with his father Abraham and his son Jacob, and described them as possessors of hands and eyes, that is, possessors of strength in obedience and penetrating insight into religion.

Isaac lived a long and blessed life, and fulfilled his Lord’s mission faithfully and sincerely.

When he grew old and his eyesight weakened, he blessed his son Jacob and prayed for his descendants and land to be blessed, and God answered his prayer.

Isaac, peace be upon him, died and was buried next to his parents, Abraham and Sarah, in the city of Hebron, Palestine, in the place known today as the Ibrahimi Mosque.

The lesson of the story of Isaac is that nothing can fail God’s power, that He provides for whomever He wills without reckoning, and that a righteous house based on monotheism produces good offspring that will benefit humanity for many centuries.
